   751→            children: The children of the component.

   761→            not self._invalid_children
   762→            and not self._valid_children

   769→            comp.__name__ for comp in (Fragment, Foreach, Cond, Match)
   770→        ]

   783→

   792→                )
   793→
   794→            if self._valid_children and child_name not in [
   795→                *self._valid_children,
   796→                *allowed_components,
   797→            ]:
   798→                valid_child_list = ", ".join(
   799→                    [f"`{v_child}`" for v_child in self._valid_children]
   800→                )
   801→                raise ValueError(
   802→                    f"The component `{comp_name}` only allows the components: {valid_child_list} as children. Got `{child_name}` instead."
   803→                )
   804→
   805→            if child._valid_parents and comp_name not in [
   806→                *child._valid_parents,
   807→                *allowed_components,
   808→            ]:
   809→                valid_parent_list = ", ".join(
   810→                    [f"`{v_parent}`" for v_parent in child._valid_parents]

   812→                raise ValueError(
   813→                    f"The component `{child_name}` can only be a child of the components: {valid_parent_list}. Got `{comp_name}` instead."

   849→        """

   852→            return vars

   855→        for _, event_vars in self._get_vars_from_event_triggers(self.event_triggers):

   860→            prop_var = getattr(self, prop)
   861→            if isinstance(prop_var, Var):

   879→            self.class_name,
   880→            self.id,
   881→            self.key,
   882→            self.autofocus,
   883→            *self.custom_attrs.values(),

   112→class VarData(Base):
   113→    """Metadata associated with a Var."""
   114→

   116→    state: str = ""
   117→
   118→    # Imports needed to render this var
   119→    imports: ImportDict = {}
   120→

   122→    hooks: Dict[str, None] = {}
   123→
   124→    # Positions of interpolated strings. This is used by the decoder to figure
   125→    # out where the interpolations are and only escape the non-interpolated
   126→    # segments.

   129→    @classmethod
   130→    def merge(cls, *others: VarData | None) -> VarData | None:
   131→        """Merge multiple var data objects.
   132→
   133→        Args:
   134→            *others: The var data objects to merge.
   135→
   136→        Returns:
   137→            The merged var data object.
   138→        """
   139→        state = ""
   140→        _imports = {}
   141→        hooks = {}
   142→        interpolations = []
   143→        for var_data in others:
   144→            if var_data is None:
   145→                continue
   146→            state = state or var_data.state
   147→            _imports = imports.merge_imports(_imports, var_data.imports)
   148→            hooks.update(var_data.hooks)
   149→            interpolations += var_data.interpolations
   150→
   151→        return (
   152→            cls(
   153→                state=state,
   154→                imports=_imports,
   155→                hooks=hooks,
   156→                interpolations=interpolations,
   157→            )
   158→            or None
   159→        )

   174→
   175→        Returns:
   176→            True if all fields are equal and collapsed imports are equal.
   177→        """

   182→        # not part of the vardata itself.

   184→            self.state == other.state

   187→            == imports.collapse_imports(other.imports)

   207→def _encode_var(value: Var) -> str:
   208→    """Encode the state name into a formatted var.
   209→
   210→    Args:
   211→        value: The value to encode the state name into.
   212→
   213→    Returns:
   214→        The encoded var.
   215→    """
   216→    if value._var_data:
   217→        from reflex.utils.serializers import serialize
   218→
   219→        final_value = str(value)
   220→        data = value._var_data.dict()
   221→        data["string_length"] = len(final_value)
   222→        data_json = value._var_data.__config__.json_dumps(data, default=serialize)
   223→
   224→        return (
   225→            f"{constants.REFLEX_VAR_OPENING_TAG}{data_json}{constants.REFLEX_VAR_CLOSING_TAG}"
   226→            + final_value
   227→        )
   228→
   229→    return str(value)

   231→
   232→# Compile regex for finding reflex var tags.
   233→_decode_var_pattern_re = (
   234→    rf"{constants.REFLEX_VAR_OPENING_TAG}(.*?){constants.REFLEX_VAR_CLOSING_TAG}"
   235→)
   236→_decode_var_pattern = re.compile(_decode_var_pattern_re, flags=re.DOTALL)
   237→
   238→
   239→def _decode_var(value: str) -> tuple[VarData | None, str]:
   240→    """Decode the state name from a formatted var.
   241→
   242→    Args:
   243→        value: The value to extract the state name from.
   244→
   245→    Returns:
   246→        The extracted state name and the value without the state name.
   247→    """
   248→    var_datas = []
   249→    if isinstance(value, str):
   250→        # fast path if there is no encoded VarData
   251→        if constants.REFLEX_VAR_OPENING_TAG not in value:
   252→            return None, value
   253→
   254→        offset = 0
   255→
   256→        # Initialize some methods for reading json.
   257→        var_data_config = VarData().__config__
   258→
   259→        def json_loads(s):
   260→            try:
   261→                return var_data_config.json_loads(s)
   262→            except json.decoder.JSONDecodeError:
   263→                return var_data_config.json_loads(var_data_config.json_loads(f'"{s}"'))
   264→
   265→        # Find all tags.
   266→        while m := _decode_var_pattern.search(value):
   267→            start, end = m.span()
   268→            value = value[:start] + value[end:]
   269→
   270→            # Read the JSON, pull out the string length, parse the rest as VarData.
   271→            data = json_loads(m.group(1))
   272→            string_length = data.pop("string_length", None)
   273→            var_data = VarData.parse_obj(data)
   274→
   275→            # Use string length to compute positions of interpolations.
   276→            if string_length is not None:
   277→                realstart = start + offset
   278→                var_data.interpolations = [(realstart, realstart + string_length)]
   279→
   280→            var_datas.append(var_data)
   281→            offset += end - start
   282→
   283→    return VarData.merge(*var_datas) if var_datas else None, value
   284→

   286→def _extract_var_data(value: Iterable) -> list[VarData | None]:
   287→    """Extract the var imports and hooks from an iterable containing a Var.
   288→
   289→    Args:
   290→        value: The iterable to extract the VarData from
   291→
   292→    Returns:
   293→        The extracted VarDatas.
   294→    """
   295→    from reflex.style import Style
   296→
   297→    var_datas = []
   298→    with contextlib.suppress(TypeError):
   299→        for sub in value:
   300→            if isinstance(sub, Var):
   301→                var_datas.append(sub._var_data)
   302→            elif not isinstance(sub, str):
   303→                # Recurse into dict values.
   304→                if hasattr(sub, "values") and callable(sub.values):
   305→                    var_datas.extend(_extract_var_data(sub.values()))
   306→                # Recurse into iterable values (or dict keys).
   307→                var_datas.extend(_extract_var_data(sub))
   308→
   309→    # Style objects should already have _var_data.
   310→    if isinstance(value, Style):
   311→        var_datas.append(value._var_data)
   312→    else:
   313→        # Recurse when value is a dict itself.
   314→        values = getattr(value, "values", None)
   315→        if callable(values):
   316→            var_datas.extend(_extract_var_data(values()))
   317→    return var_datas

   341→    @classmethod
   342→    def create(
   343→        cls, value: Any, _var_is_local: bool = True, _var_is_string: bool = False
   344→    ) -> Var | None:
   345→        """Create a var from a value.
   346→
   347→        Args:
   348→            value: The value to create the var from.
   349→            _var_is_local: Whether the var is local.
   350→            _var_is_string: Whether the var is a string literal.
   351→
   352→        Returns:
   353→            The var.
   354→

   356→            TypeError: If the value is JSON-unserializable.
   357→        """
   358→        # Check for none values.
   359→        if value is None:
   360→            return None
   361→
   362→        # If the value is already a var, do nothing.
   363→        if isinstance(value, Var):
   364→            return value
   365→
   366→        # Try to pull the imports and hooks from contained values.
   367→        _var_data = None
   368→        if not isinstance(value, str):
   369→            _var_data = VarData.merge(*_extract_var_data(value))
   370→
   371→        # Try to serialize the value.
   372→        type_ = type(value)
   373→        name = value if type_ in types.JSONType else serializers.serialize(value)
   374→        if name is None:
   375→            raise TypeError(
   376→                f"No JSON serializer found for var {value} of type {type_}."
   377→            )
   378→        name = name if isinstance(name, str) else format.json_dumps(name)
   379→
   380→        return BaseVar(
   381→            _var_name=name,
   382→            _var_type=type_,
   383→            _var_is_local=_var_is_local,
   384→            _var_is_string=_var_is_string,
   385→            _var_data=_var_data,

   577→    def __getitem__(self, i: Any) -> Var:
   578→        """Index into a var.
   579→
   580→        Args:
   581→            i: The index to index into.
   582→

   584→            The indexed var.
   585→
   586→        Raises:
   587→            TypeError: If the var is not indexable.
   588→        """
   589→        # Indexing is only supported for strings, lists, tuples, dicts, and dataframes.
   590→        if not (
   591→            types._issubclass(self._var_type, Union[List, Dict, Tuple, str])
   592→            or types.is_dataframe(self._var_type)
   593→        ):
   594→            if self._var_type == Any:
   595→                raise TypeError(
   596→                    "Could not index into var of type Any. (If you are trying to index into a state var, "
   597→                    "add the correct type annotation to the var.)"
   598→                )
   599→            raise TypeError(
   600→                f"Var {self._var_name} of type {self._var_type} does not support indexing."
   601→            )
   602→
   603→        # The type of the indexed var.
   604→        type_ = Any
   605→
   606→        # Convert any vars to local vars.
   607→        if isinstance(i, Var):
   608→            i = i._replace(_var_is_local=True)
   609→
   610→        # Handle list/tuple/str indexing.
   611→        if types._issubclass(self._var_type, Union[List, Tuple, str]):
   612→            # List/Tuple/String indices must be ints, slices, or vars.
   613→            if (
   614→                not isinstance(i, types.get_args(Union[int, slice, Var]))
   615→                or isinstance(i, Var)
   616→                and not i._var_type == int
   617→            ):
   618→                raise TypeError("Index must be an integer or an integer var.")
   619→
   620→            # Handle slices first.
   621→            if isinstance(i, slice):
   622→                # Get the start and stop indices.
   623→                start = i.start or 0
   624→                stop = i.stop or "undefined"
   625→
   626→                # Use the slice function.
   627→                return self._replace(
   628→                    _var_name=f"{self._var_name}.slice({start}, {stop})",
   629→                    _var_is_string=False,
   630→                )
   631→
   632→            # Get the type of the indexed var.
   633→            if types.is_generic_alias(self._var_type):
   634→                index = i if not isinstance(i, Var) else 0
   635→                type_ = types.get_args(self._var_type)
   636→                type_ = type_[index % len(type_)] if type_ else Any
   637→            elif types._issubclass(self._var_type, str):
   638→                type_ = str
   639→
   640→            # Use `at` to support negative indices.
   641→            return self._replace(
   642→                _var_name=f"{self._var_name}.at({i})",
   643→                _var_type=type_,
   644→                _var_is_string=False,
   645→            )
   646→
   647→        # Dictionary / dataframe indexing.
   648→        # Tuples are currently not supported as indexes.
   649→        if (
   650→            (
   651→                types._issubclass(self._var_type, Dict)
   652→                or types.is_dataframe(self._var_type)
   653→            )
   654→            and not isinstance(i, types.get_args(Union[int, str, float, Var]))
   655→        ) or (
   656→            isinstance(i, Var)
   657→            and not types._issubclass(
   658→                i._var_type, types.get_args(Union[int, str, float])
   659→            )
   660→        ):
   661→            raise TypeError(
   662→                "Index must be one of the following types: int, str, int or str Var"
   663→            )
   664→        # Get the type of the indexed var.
   665→        if isinstance(i, str):
   666→            i = format.wrap(i, '"')
   667→        type_ = (
   668→            types.get_args(self._var_type)[1]
   669→            if types.is_generic_alias(self._var_type)
   670→            else Any
   671→        )
   672→
   673→        # Use normal indexing here.
   674→        return self._replace(
   675→            _var_name=f"{self._var_name}[{i}]",
   676→            _var_type=type_,
   677→            _var_is_string=False,
   678→        )

  1881→
  1882→        Returns:
  1883→            The value of the var for the given instance.
  1884→        """
  1885→        if instance is None or not self._cache:
  1886→            return super().__get__(instance, owner)

  1889→        if not hasattr(instance, self._cache_attr):
  1890→            setattr(instance, self._cache_attr, super().__get__(instance, owner))
  1891→            # Ensure the computed var gets serialized to redis.
  1892→            instance._was_touched = True

  1895→    def _deps(
  1896→        self,
  1897→        objclass: Type,
  1898→        obj: FunctionType | CodeType | None = None,
  1899→        self_name: Optional[str] = None,
  1900→    ) -> set[str]:
  1901→        """Determine var dependencies of this ComputedVar.
  1902→
  1903→        Save references to attributes accessed on "self".  Recursively called
  1904→        when the function makes a method call on "self" or define comprehensions
  1905→        or nested functions that may reference "self".
  1906→
  1907→        Args:
  1908→            objclass: the class obj this ComputedVar is attached to.
  1909→            obj: the object to disassemble (defaults to the fget function).
  1910→            self_name: if specified, look for this name in LOAD_FAST and LOAD_DEREF instructions.
  1911→
  1912→        Returns:
  1913→            A set of variable names accessed by the given obj.
  1914→
  1915→        Raises:
  1916→            ValueError: if the function references the get_state, parent_state, or substates attributes
  1917→                (cannot track deps in a related state, only implicitly via parent state).
  1918→        """
  1919→        d = set()
  1920→        if obj is None:
  1921→            fget = property.__getattribute__(self, "fget")
  1922→            if fget is not None:
  1923→                obj = cast(FunctionType, fget)
  1924→            else:
  1925→                return set()
  1926→        with contextlib.suppress(AttributeError):
  1927→            # unbox functools.partial
  1928→            obj = cast(FunctionType, obj.func)  # type: ignore
  1929→        with contextlib.suppress(AttributeError):
  1930→            # unbox EventHandler
  1931→            obj = cast(FunctionType, obj.fn)  # type: ignore
  1932→
  1933→        if self_name is None and isinstance(obj, FunctionType):
  1934→            try:
  1935→                # the first argument to the function is the name of "self" arg
  1936→                self_name = obj.__code__.co_varnames[0]
  1937→            except (AttributeError, IndexError):
  1938→                self_name = None
  1939→        if self_name is None:
  1940→            # cannot reference attributes on self if method takes no args
  1941→            return set()
  1942→
  1943→        invalid_names = ["get_state", "parent_state", "substates", "get_substate"]
  1944→        self_is_top_of_stack = False
  1945→        for instruction in dis.get_instructions(obj):
  1946→            if (
  1947→                instruction.opname in ("LOAD_FAST", "LOAD_DEREF")
  1948→                and instruction.argval == self_name
  1949→            ):
  1950→                # bytecode loaded the class instance to the top of stack, next load instruction
  1951→                # is referencing an attribute on self
  1952→                self_is_top_of_stack = True
  1953→                continue
  1954→            if self_is_top_of_stack and instruction.opname in (
  1955→                "LOAD_ATTR",
  1956→                "LOAD_METHOD",
  1957→            ):
  1958→                try:
  1959→                    ref_obj = getattr(objclass, instruction.argval)
  1960→                except Exception:
  1961→                    ref_obj = None
  1962→                if instruction.argval in invalid_names:
  1963→                    raise ValueError(
  1964→                        f"Cached var {self._var_full_name} cannot access arbitrary state via `{instruction.argval}`."
  1965→                    )
  1966→                if callable(ref_obj):
  1967→                    # recurse into callable attributes
  1968→                    d.update(
  1969→                        self._deps(
  1970→                            objclass=objclass,
  1971→                            obj=ref_obj,
  1972→                        )
  1973→                    )
  1974→                else:
  1975→                    # normal attribute access
  1976→                    d.add(instruction.argval)
  1977→            elif instruction.opname == "LOAD_CONST" and isinstance(
  1978→                instruction.argval, CodeType
  1979→            ):
  1980→                # recurse into nested functions / comprehensions, which can reference
  1981→                # instance attributes from the outer scope
  1982→                d.update(
  1983→                    self._deps(
  1984→                        objclass=objclass,
  1985→                        obj=instruction.argval,
  1986→                        self_name=self_name,
  1987→                    )
  1988→                )
  1989→            self_is_top_of_stack = False
  1990→        return d

  2022→        fget: The getter function.
  2023→        initial_value: The initial value of the computed var.
  2024→        cache: Whether to cache the computed value.
  2025→        **kwargs: additional attributes to set on the instance
  2026→

  2028→        A ComputedVar instance.

  2035→            fget=fget,

  2037→            cache=cache,
  2038→            **kwargs,

text: Here’s what I did to address the issue and improve the error message clarity when a non-string is passed to a Literal-typed component prop like Heading.size: Summary of the problem - When a component prop is annotated with a Literal (e.g., size: Literal["1","2",...,"9"]), passing a non-string value like an int 9 triggers a ValueError, but the message only shows the disallowed value with quotes (Got '9' instead), which is misleading and doesn’t mention the type mismatch (int vs str). Fix implemented - Updated the error message generated by validate_literal in reflex/utils/types.py to explicitly include both the expected literal’s type and the actual value’s type. This makes it clear when a type mismatch is the reason for the error. Change details - File modified: /testbed/reflex/utils/types.py - Function: validate_literal - Old message: prop value for size of the `Heading` component should be one of the following: '1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8','9'. Got '9' instead - New message: prop value for size of the `Heading` component should be one of the following: '1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8','9' (type str). Got 9 of type int instead This is the exact change applied: - Added expected literal type name and the actual type to the exception message. - Avoided quoting the “Got” value unless it is a string, so Got 9 of type int reads naturally. Reproduction test I added a focused test that reproduces the issue using the Radix Themes Heading component (whose size prop uses LiteralTextSize of "1"–"9") and verifies the improved error message: - New test file: /testbed/tests/components/typography/test_heading_literal_error.py - Test code: import pytest from reflex.components.radix.themes.typography.heading import Heading def test_heading_size_literal_type_error(): """Passing an int to Heading.size should raise a ValueError with type info.""" with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo: Heading.create(size=9) msg = str(excinfo.value) assert "should be one of the following" in msg # Expect the message to indicate the allowed literal type and the received type assert "(type str)" in msg assert "Got 9 of type int" in msg Notes on running tests - In this environment pytest and some external dependencies (like rich, used by reflex.utils.console) are not installed, so I couldn’t run the test here. - Locally, to run the tests: 1. Ensure dependencies are installed: pytest, rich (and any others required by Reflex in this repository). - pip install pytest rich 2. Run: pytest tests/components/typography/test_heading_literal_error.py -q - The test checks that the error message includes the expected literal type and the actual type, making the message clear when a non-string (like int) is passed. Why this fixes the bug - The underlying validation pathway already checks Literals and throws a ValueError when the value is not one of allowed Literal args (validate_literal is invoked in Component.__init__). - The bug was in the error message formatting, not in the type checking itself. The improved message now explicitly calls out the expected type (str for string Literals) and the actual type (int in this example), addressing the user’s complaint.
